reviews.title: The links are way too easy to trigger
reviews.text: The WP app is good, but when you scroll an article and your thumb hits a link to an advertisement, the add opens way too easily. It’s an annoyance.

I just purchased a subscription in app . I cannot read or listen to articles in full without annoying “Election Day “

reviews.title: Little Remains of the Real WaPo
reviews.text: The paper gets worse every week. Reporting is biased, editorials are advertorials. WaPo has sold out and it shows.

reviews.title: Doctors charging ….
reviews.text:
Horrific title belting reality that harms so many …. To grab reader’s attention?  Editorial board discretion now under suspicion.  
Maintain clear standards and avoid sensationalism.  Article is an affront to those who tirelessly function for the good of patients while the minority (how many IS the issue) who should not be docs but are money grubbing fiends.
Editorial standards have been violated.  For everyone’s benefit, acknowledge the obvious mistake and go on if you intend on not being tarred by the same brush.  Seek the higher morality and reach for better.  Thank you.

reviews.title: A National Tragedy
reviews.text: Washington Post is a shell of its former self. Most local news and sports come from wire services.  Editorials are pro-Trump right-wing drivel. Bezos needs to sell the paper to someone with journalism ethics.

reviews.title: Remove side scrolling!
reviews.text: The makers of this app need to remove side scrolling between articles. This feature greatly harms the reader experience by causing accidental switching to another article while trying to scroll downwards to continue reading.

reviews.title: WP Headlines Trump as Peacemaker & In So Doing Joins Trump in Betraying Ukraine and Democracy
reviews.text:
Your journalistic piece relegating Russia’s attack on Ukraine and it’s continuing war crimes against Ukraine… into a feud between Zelinsky, who is defending his country’s very survival, and Donald Trump, who has allied himself with the attacker and war criminal Vladimir Putin, is not doing the work of a free press, but rather perpetuating the propaganda of Donald Trump
And Putin . Shame on you. A sad day for the Washington Post.
Now to unsubscribe . Anything else I just sit down to unsubscribe?

reviews.title: Tiny text
reviews.text: Why is the text so small? Other news apps are much more readable witu larger size.  They are all using my default iPadOS settings so don’t tell me I need to adjust those  and impact all.

reviews.title: No Kings Day coverage
reviews.text: Your coverage of this important nationwide event was minimal and seems to have been deliberately suppressed.  This will be an important consideration when it comes time to renew my subscription.

reviews.title: Leaving the Washington Post for Good
reviews.text: We have been Post subscribers since we moved to the DC area in our 20’s. For 40+ years we have read great stories crafted by excellent reporters.  But now we are leaving the Post for the Washington Sun.  We are tired of the sycophantic coverage of Trump and Elon Musk…people who will stop at nothing to enrich themselves at the expense of others.  The editorial celebrating Musk for his flying car when he is literally killing people in Ukraine through his disabling of Starlink was the final straw. Do you have no sense of decency left there in that building that once housed the greats in the news industry.  Bezos should be ashamed at what he has ‘accomplished’ here, but at least he gets to keep his government money rolling in.  A pox on all your houses.

reviews.title: The unfriendly ghost
reviews.text: Sports page is a ghost of former self. Outdated stories.  Outdated results. I only read it for the TV listings and sometimes they are wrong

reviews.title: An American Institution Torpedoed
reviews.text: Once a foundational news source for the city, region, and country, The Post, much in line with the democracy, is now a depleted shell of itself.  Abandoning (and firing) some of the best writing and editing in the history of journalism in favor of sidling up to a wannabe dictator.  The owner has the wealth and influence to do enormous good in the world, but greed and vanity truly seem to be an insurmountable human barriers.  And, as history has shown, cowardice breeds oppression. The Post is now yet another unfortunate victim of that cowardice.

reviews.title: If you pay your bill, the Post still cut off your access!
reviews.text: I received the Post digitally these days.  I have been a Post reader for more than 30 years.  In the past two years the Post has cut my subscription over 17 times and I finally decided I was too frustrated and it  got cancelled about a month ago .  Now they want me to resubscribe?  If they cared they would still have me as a customer.

reviews.title: Total BS that Gift Articles now require a recipient to create an account?!?
reviews.text: I would have happily given 5 stars, but I just shared a gift link and clicked on it to see what it was like- and to my surprise my “gift” could only be redeemed if the recipient provided an email address and opened an account with WaPo. Not cool!!

reviews.title: Prompts user to update iOS
reviews.text: The app and publication are good.  But the app pesters the user to update iOS.  I am running a supported version 18.7.8 and have no need to update.   I am considering cancelling my subscription if this isn’t corrected.

reviews.title: Democracy Survives with Trusted Balanced Editorials
reviews.text: Mr. Bezos and conservative columnists like Marc Thiessen have defended balanced changes. Mr. Bezos argues that ending endorsements and realignment of the opinion section's reduces institutional bias.  The editorial board now fosters "hyper-independence",  and away from political opinions thus calming voter anxiety and working toward restoration of the broad public trust in the legacy media. Voters are looking for creative ideas to solve issues. Then ask the readers for real technical solutions.

reviews.title: Hate the WP
reviews.text: The ownership stinks.  The Post has the best reporting after Politico, but the ownership is ruining it.  Every day I scan the NY Times and think “who cares?” “who cares” and “who cares?”  The Times almost never reports on anything of importance.  The Post, on the other hand, reports on everything of importance, much of it original/exclusive.  Yet all the subscribers are leaving due to the moronic “opinions” the Post is forced to print (or in some cases not print).  And the stupid tech issues the Post never fixes.  Updating to add—the Post developers must be the dumbest people on earth.  No one has noticed that the comment format for Hax columns is totally unlike the comment sections anywhere else in the app (you can’t sort by oldest first).  And now the report function doesn’t work, so the comments are filling up with troll garbage.  I’m glad I got my subscription at a reduced rate, because as much as I want to support the Post (despite its leadership), there’s no way I’m paying full price for this.
